# Backspace Fork 1.16.3

Juno gets a new cosmic interface, persistent space rankings and clearer call-game
navigation, while retaining the existing authoritative game and voice lifecycle.

## New and improved

- Original locally served card fronts/back, cosmic table, player frames and
  result artwork, with real Backspace names, space nicknames and avatars.
- Responsive lobby, table, results and ranking screens. Side hands now expose
  distinct, spaced card backs and a larger exact remaining-card count.
- Persistent **Juno XP per space**, shared across its voice channels: places
  1–4 earn **120 / 80 / 40 / 20 XP**. Remaining-card counts after final penalties
  determine places; ties share competition ranks and XP (`1, 2, 2, 4`).
- Paginated space rankings include wins, completed rounds and your own position,
  even off-page. Spectators, early departures and rounds without a winner earn
  no XP or completed-round/win increments.
- Atomic, once-per-round credits survive restart. Failed credit remains pending
  for retry and blocks a rematch instead of silently losing or doubling awards.
- One shared **Games** picker in sidebar, desktop mosaic and mobile controls.
  Opening/canceling the picker or viewing rankings does not join/leave a game.
- The sidebar RNNoise control sits beside Disconnect, separate from microphone
  mute. Updated game/result/ranking copy is included in all five languages.

## Operations and compatibility

- Includes additive migration **0048** for Juno round results, participants and
  space totals. Back up the database/uploads before upgrading; normal startup
  applies migrations through the existing pre-migration snapshot flow.
- Channel deletion preserves credited space XP. Leaving/rejoining retains it;
  account deletion erases personal progression. Authorized account reattachment
  deduplicates round awards before consolidating totals, including a round whose
  credit is pending while the identities are merged.
- The hosting instance owns identities, game state and rankings. Other spaces
  and instances remain independent; no new S2S score relay or dependency.
- Old Juno hosts can omit scoreboards; an unsupported ranking is shown as
  unavailable rather than invented XP. DM games remain unsupported.
- Active tables and unconfirmed rounds remain ephemeral across host restart;
  committed XP is durable. No historical games receive retroactive awards.
- Acceptance includes real HTTP/WebSocket gameplay, SQLite rollback/retry,
  restart and two-instance identity isolation, plus controlled desktop/mobile/
  short/scaled UI checks. Multi-device LiveKit media and native fullscreen Escape
  were not validated by those tests.
- Publication does **not** deploy to or restart an existing server. The supplied
  artwork is published with the project user's explicit authorization; provenance
  and source hashes are recorded alongside the assets.
